Definition: from G2875; blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb):--deaf, dumb, speechless.
KeyPassages: Matthew 9:32; Matthew 9:33; Matthew 11:5; Matthew 12:22; Mark 7:32; Luke 1:22
BiblicalUsage: Kophos means blunted, and so deaf or dumb. Matthew 9:32 brings a dumb man possessed with a devil, and Matthew 9:33 has the dumb speaking when the devil is cast out, Matthew 11:5 lists the deaf hearing among the signs of the Messiah, Matthew 12:22 heals a man blind and dumb, both speaking and seeing, Mark 7:32 brings one deaf with an impediment in his speech, and Luke 1:22 leaves Zacharias speechless after his vision in the temple.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the deaf and dumb are the Messiah's own signs: the blind see, the deaf hear, and the dumb speak, because the kingdom has come. I hold that Zacharias was made speechless for not believing, and the dumb man was made to speak for believing, and the difference is faith.
